item.title: Carbon Monoxide Detector Placement: Where to Install (and Where Not To)
item.description:
You bought a carbon monoxide detector. You took it out of the box. But where exactly should you put it?

Placement matters more than most people think. A CO detector in the wrong location won’t detect carbon monoxide in time to warn you — and since CO is odorless, colorless, and invisible, you won’t know it’s there until the alarm sounds (or until it’s too late).

This guide covers the exact placement rules, room-by-room recommendations, and the common mistakes that make CO detectors less effective.

item.title: Fire Extinguisher Mounting Height and Placement: A Simple Home Guide
item.description:
Placement matters as much as extinguisher type. A well-placed extinguisher is easy to reach, visible, and safe to use. This guide explains practical mounting height and placement tips for homes without getting overly technical.

Problem Explanation

If a fire starts, you need to reach an extinguisher quickly. Placement should make it easy to grab without getting too close to the fire. A great extinguisher in a bad location is less useful than a good one placed well.
